subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw keep this broad multi-agent collaboration RFC as a core roadmap umbrella, narrow it into specific canonical trackers, or reject the full core stack in favor of plugin/API-only extension points?
rationale: The requested stack adds core orchestration, memory visibility, persistent state, budget config, and security-sensitive delegation behavior, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Keep as umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broad product/security umbrella and use narrower issues for implementation-ready slices.

options.title: Split into trackers
options.body: Create or bless separate canonical trackers for capability routing, blackboard/search, memory visibility, and budget admission, then close this umbrella once links preserve the discussion.

options.title: Reject core stack
options.body: Close this direction for core and ask contributors to pursue plugin or ClawHub experiments unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Keep as umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broad product/security umbrella and use narrower issues for implementation-ready slices.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from CODEOWNERS, related RFC scoping, and recent central-path history.
